executiveSummary: GM0995's identity, Flevoland province and Flevoland safety-region assignment are coherent. The fresh 2025 full boundary contains the generated centre and CBS reports 84,713 residents; 136 neighbourhood rows sum to 84,710 (-3, -0.004%), a negligible annual rounding/suppression difference. The bundle contains eleven districts, 136 neighbourhoods, one BAG place and two BRT settlement records. The BAG place label falls outside the independently versioned generalized boundary but the simulation centre remains inside the full boundary; this is a geometry-edition/generalization caveat, not exclusion of Lelystad. Eight logical road records represent six physical corridors because A6 and N307 each appear at two municipal sides; those sections are not additive redundancy. Lelystad Centrum station and 114 scheduled-transit stop areas are present. All ten presets execute deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services and pass structural/numerical contracts. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Official evidence distinguishes IJsselmeer/Markermeer primary-defence breach, prolonged polder drainage through Lage Vaart and gemaal Wortman, local cloudburst flow/storage, and buitendijkse exposure. The generic river preset selects none of those cases but holds 0.994441 normalized inundation stress through T+72 and accumulates 2,146,148 person-hours. Eight unrelated single-hazard presets reuse exactly the same full neighbourhood rank. Moving the wildfire source into Hollandse Hout leaves the containing neighbourhood 134th of 136, while source-remote canonical fire produces only smoke and the same generic ordering. Current Houtribsluis water and KNMI observations are context, not evidence for the synthetic scenarios. Future Houtribdijk heavy-vehicle restrictions and planned commercial/military airport use must not be promoted to current state. Lelystad has no full emergency department or ICU; serious cases depend on cross-boundary Harderwijk/Almere routes. Exact utilities, care, mobility, supply and first-72-hour recovery remain unsupported by live topology, state, resources and actions. Unknown/NoData never means zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.title: E01 — Kerncijfers wijken en buurten 2025, table 86165NED, OData API
supports: The official municipality row identifies GM0995 Lelystad and reports 84,713 residents, density 370 per square kilometre, 18.3% age 65 or older and 13,184 one-person households.

The 136 published neighbourhood rows sum to 84,710 residents (-3, -0.004%), 37,170 households and 15,530 residents aged 65 or older; the negligible difference retains annual rounding and suppression semantics.

Population and core age/household fields cover all 136 neighbourhoods. Home-value/tenure and benefit fields cover only 84–87; doctor/supermarket distance and density cover 98; district heating and public charging cover zero and must remain Unknown/NoData.

CBS OData is machine-readable under CC BY 4.0, with quarterly additions described for this annual table. It controls residents, not incident-time visitors, pupils, patients, workers, airport users, responders, individual vulnerability or preparedness.

evidenceSources.publisher: PDOK / CBS / Kadaster / Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi
evidenceSources.title: E02 — Full municipal geometry, settlement and road, rail and scheduled-transit reference inputs
evidenceSources.edition: 2025 boundary/statistics and current generated BAG, BRT, NWB, ProRail and GTFS snapshots
supports: The generated centre [5.432065007512449, 52.474315569247295] lies inside the fresh full-resolution 2025 municipal boundary.

The bundle retains eleven districts, 136 neighbourhoods, one BAG place and two BRT records: Lelystad and Lelystad-Haven. The BAG label point lies outside the independently versioned generalized boundary, requiring a water-rich/coastal generalization caveat rather than reassignment.

Eight logical boundary records collapse to six physical corridors: A6, N302, N307, N701, N706 and N309. The two A6 and two N307 sides serve different directions along the same corridors and are not additive independent capacity.

Lelystad Centrum is the sole ProRail station inside GM0995 and 114 GTFS stop areas are assigned. Static geometry and timetables do not prove incident-time road, bridge, rail or bus operation, access, destination or throughput.

CBS boundary OGC is half-yearly/CC BY 4.0; BAG is daily/Public Domain Mark 1.0; BRT is CC BY 4.0; NWB is monthly/CC0 1.0; ProRail is manually refreshed/CC0 1.0. OVapi GTFS is free-use best-effort context without an operational SLA.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Lelystadse Adaptatiestrategie 2023 and Gemeentelijk Rioleringsprogramma 2022–2031
supports: The strategy says 70 mm in one hour or 100 mm in two hours leaves more than 30 cm in places and can make Stationsdreef and Lindelaan inaccessible to emergency services; its southwest example identifies bedrijventerrein Noordersluis.

It states that local differences require place-specific treatment across water nuisance, heat and drought and identifies businesses/vital functions as exposed to water and heat disruption. These are stress-test/planning statements, not incident observations.

The sewer programme describes a historically spacious stormwater/surface-water system, but requires current stress-test checks, surface routing to safe low storage and delayed drainage/infiltration. Its service goals include keeping main roads, emergency traffic and vital functions available.

Programmes and design goals do not prove incident-time rain, sewer/inlet/storage capacity, blocked drains, street flow, road passability, pump state or completed action. Native model edition, hyetograph, CRS, resolution, uncertainty, licence and NoData remain required for analytical use.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Gemaal Wortman, IJsselmeer/Oostvaardersdijk work and public GM0995 water assets
evidenceSources.edition: Current water-board pages; HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: Gemaal Wortman pumps Lage Vaart polder water about four metres upward into Markermeer, including continual seepage. Zuiderzeeland publishes target levels -6.20 m NAP for Lage Vaart and -5.20 m NAP for Hoge Vaart and four pumps of 500 m³/min each; the diesel installation requires operational interpretation.

The HWH snapshot assigns 89 objects to GM0995: eight sewer pumps, six surface-water pumps, 71 weirs, three sluices and AWZI Lelystad. It includes Wortman at 33.333 capacity, consistent with 2,000 m³/min only if the native unit is retained, not inferred from a normalized field.

The IJsselmeerdijk between Lelystad and Ketelbrug is in a 17 km strengthening project; Zuiderzeeland says it is currently safe while future standards require strengthening. Oostvaardersdijk is under separate investigation. Planned work is not a failure, completed protection or live defence state.

No public registry establishes full catchment/defence connectivity, IJsselmeer/Markermeer boundary, Lage/Hoge Vaart levels, asset command, blockage, power/fuel/manual staffing, maintenance, backup, current state or T+72 restoration. HWH aggregation is partial/contributor-dependent under CC BY-SA 4.0.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2024, published flood plans, LIWO and first-72-hour preparedness
evidenceSources.edition: Definitive RRP 2024; published 2009 flood coordination/evacuation plans retained as dated doctrine; LIWO 2025.1.6
supports: The 2024 profile ranks flooding as a high-impact Flevoland risk because warning and early-evacuation opportunity are shorter and water remains longer due to the volume requiring pumping. It makes nature fire a priority while stating the detailed Flevoland inventory was incomplete.

The still-published 2009 coordination plan separates primary-defence breach, extreme/long rain and buitendijkse flooding, places Lelystad/Dronten in zone Midden and models approximately two days of filling after a selected extreme case. Its old population, infrastructure and probability assumptions are dated doctrine, not current scenario truth.

LIWO is a professional scenario system requiring specialist interpretation. A usable flood case must retain source, defence/breach, footprint, depth/velocity units/datum, arrival/duration/recession, probability, CRS/resolution, edition, licence and NoData; it is not a live observation by default.

National guidance advises a 72-hour kit including three litres of water per person per day, food, medicine, radio/power and a personal plan. Guidance does not prove household readiness, municipal stock or distribution capacity.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Oostvaardersplassen, Hollandse Hout and Lelystad stadsbossen
evidenceSources.edition: Current area/access pages and 2025 annual report accessed 3 September 2026
supports: Oostvaardersplassen is a 7,500-hectare wetland/nature complex between Almere and Lelystad; Hollandse Hout, Kotterbos, Oostvaardersbos and Oostvaardersveld are component areas with public access and recreation.

Staatsbosbeheer identifies four Lelystad city forests, including Zuigerplasbos, Gelderse Hout and Visvijverbos around/through urban and A6 edges. These establish fuel, smoke, access and visitor eligibility, not an ignition or exact occupancy.
The 2025 report records at least 588,613 visits at Poort Oostvaardersplassen Lelystad before December completion, showing material non-resident demand; an annual counter is not event-time presence.
The public pages do not establish current official fire phase, fuel moisture, ignition/perimeter, wind/plume, access closure, firewater, suppression resources or T+72 containment.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / Rijksoverheid / Lelystad Airport / Veiligheidsregio Flevoland
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Houtribdijk lifecycle, Lelystad Airport current/future state and airport planning
evidenceSources.edition: RWS notice issued 27 August 2026; national airport decision 17 April 2026; RBP v2.07 provisionally adopted 3 July 2024
supports: Rijkswaterstaat announced that an axle/total-weight restriction of 7.3/15 tonnes will begin on Houtribdijk in autumn 2026 because Houtrib bridge structures are vulnerable; heavy vehicles will detour while emergency services and vans can continue. No exact start date is published, so it is future/planned on 3 September, not active.

The N307 Houtribdijk is a long cross-water road/bridge/sluice lifeline to Enkhuizen. A 150-unit scenario ceiling and empty NDW screen do not encode vehicle weight, bridge state, detour length or live passage.

The national government says the current airport decision permits civil but not commercial flights and targets conditional commercial opening in October 2027. Lelystad Airport reports current General Aviation operation around 80,000 annual movements and regular 07:00–22:00 hours; future passenger/F-35 plans are not current operations.

VRF's public RBP v2.07 was provisionally adopted in July 2024 and protected operational detail remains non-public. A plan validates airport incident relevance, not an incident, current occupants, aircraft/fuel state, responders or resource availability.

evidenceSources.title: E08 — Lelystad limited urgent care and cross-boundary emergency-department dependency
evidenceSources.edition: Current hospital pages; RIVM acute-care questionnaire 2026 v1.1
supports: St Jansdal states that Lelystad's Spoedpoli is for referred, non-life-threatening/light urgent care, open Monday–Friday 08:00–16:00, and that Lelystad has no intensive care or full emergency department.

For serious care ambulances go directly to another hospital, for example Harderwijk or Almere. This creates a cross-boundary route, ambulance, destination/acceptance and capacity dependency absent from a municipal Facilities scalar.
The RIVM screen correctly assigns zero full acute-care locations inside GM0995. That is not zero healthcare, zero demand or proof that external emergency care is available.

Public facility/opening facts do not establish incident-time staffing, appointments, occupancy, HAP operation, acceptance/diversion, ambulance availability, generator/fuel, medicines, supplies or restoration. RIVM v1.1 is CC0 1.0.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / KNMI / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO
evidenceSources.title: E09 — Timestamped water/weather observations and public grid, antenna and education screens
supports: Waterinfo observed -25 cm NAP at Houtribsluis south at 17:30Z on 2 September and forecast -23, -21, -23 and -19 cm NAP through T+24. No assigned T+48/T+72 point remains; this is point boundary context, not defence state or inundation, and absent horizons remain NoData.

KNMI has two 23:30Z observations inside GM0995: Houtribdijk has 11.13 m/s gust with temperature/rain unavailable; Lelystad Airport reports 17.4 °C, 5.81 m/s gust and zero last-hour rain. Ten-minute observations are not scenario forcing or a 72-hour forecast.

One postcode sample, 8245AA, maps to Liander OS ZUIDERVELD 10-1i: withdrawal existing/required/queue 69/80/22.5 MW with 83 requests, injection 69/55/83 MW with 40 requests, 28 projects and earliest year 2029. Planning is not municipal coverage, live load, feeder topology or outage.

The screens contain 178 RDI sites—82 mobile, 48 fixed-link, 41 amateur, five other-mobile and two broadcast—and 68 DUO records—39 primary, five secondary, eight special and sixteen other. Registers do not establish coverage/backhaul/power, occupants, shelter role, supplies or operation.

Waterinfo is CC0/public point context; KNMI is CC BY 4.0 at ten-minute cadence; DUO's 31 August snapshot is daily under CC Attribution version unspecified; RDI cadence/licence is unstated. All remain affectsSimulation=false.

identity.summary: GM0995, Lelystad, Flevoland and Veiligheidsregio Flevoland are internally and officially coherent.
notes: Generated municipality, province and exactly one safety-region assignment agree.
The representative centre lies inside the fresh full-resolution 2025 boundary.
Annual registers, static plans/assets, timestamped observations, forecasts, official scenarios and synthetic outputs remain distinct evidence classes.

geography.summary: Administrative geography is usable with a generalization caveat, but flood, pluvial, heat, fire/smoke, cyber and infrastructure geography does not govern impacts.
notes: The BAG place label lies outside the generalized polygon in this water-rich municipality; full boundary and centre checks pass, so analytical containment must pin geometry edition/resolution.
Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire share exactly the same full 136-neighbourhood T+24 severity order.
River selects no IJsselmeer/Markermeer defence breach, Lage/Hoge Vaart boundary, terrain-connected footprint, arrival or recession; pluvial lacks the official street-flow/storage mechanisms.
A controlled ignition inside Hollandse Hout leaves the containing neighbourhood rank 134/136, disproving source-containment plausibility.

demography.summary: Official resident controls and neighbourhood aggregates reconcile within negligible CBS rounding/suppression difference.
notes: CBS reports 84,713 residents; 136 rows sum to 84,710 (-3, -0.004%), while model allocations reconcile to the municipality control.
The 18.3% age-65-plus share and 13,184 one-person households inform aggregate heat/outage/welfare pressure but never identify individual need or preparedness.
Residents remain separate from nature visitors, airport users/staff, pupils, St Jansdal patients/staff, commuters, workers and responders under CORR-015.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at all six mandatory checkpoints for all eight services.
notes: The initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM0995 pnpm audit:model gate passed one file/two tests in 30.59 seconds; structural execution does not establish local calibration.

notes: Outputs expose hazard, direct-service, interdependency, network, recovery and local-allocation components with matched totals.
Cumulative person-hours are synthetic no-event counterfactual accounting, not observed outage duration, casualties, displaced people or unmet care.
No selected breach/rain/fire/cyber/airport event, pump/dike/road action, operator network or external hospital acceptance explains exact trajectories.
Each state change requires authority/owner, target, prerequisite, route, crew/material/fuel/water, start/end, state, evidence class/time and uncertainty.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent flood/compound disruption and exact recovery lack incident, action, constraint and resource evidence through T+72.
notes: River severity/stress and seven services remain fixed T+24–72, affected grows 22,285 to 24,753 and Facilities falls 0.667794 to 0.520120, accumulating 2,146,148.373 person-hours without selected breach, recession/pumping or action.

Compound severity/cyber decline while pressure, stress, approximately 49,747 affected and seven services remain exactly fixed; Supply changes only 0.823658 to 0.823696, accumulating 3,466,502.604 person-hours without resources.

Storm/pluvial/winter/wildfire direct effects return to zero with exact residual services; heat severity persists but affected becomes zero, and coastal has no direct water yet accumulates 357,330.754 person-hours. Earthquake accumulates 111,127.576 despite no T+24/72 ground motion or affected people.
Sustained disruption can be plausible, but exact first-72-hour deterioration, plateau and recovery require selected events, measured/modelled state, constraints, resources and actions.

findings.summary: Persistent generic river flooding lacks a selected IJsselmeer/Markermeer defence breach or Flevoland water case.
findings.evidence: River T+24/T+72 both report severity 0.306826 and normalized inundation stress 0.994441, with affected growing 22,285 to 24,753. Official sources distinguish IJsselmeer/Markermeer primary-defence breach, extreme/long rain, buitendijkse areas and Lage/Hoge Vaart drainage, and say breach water can remain because very large volumes require pumping. The run selects no water boundary, dike section/failure, Knardijk/sluice state, footprint, depth/velocity, arrival or recession. Coastal direct water zero is only a scoped North Sea result, not flood safety.
findings.action: Suppress unsupported local river precision. Enable direct inundation only for an expert-selected, versioned Zuiderzeeland/WMCN/LIWO case retaining source, defence/breach, compartment/control state, terrain-connected footprint, units/datum, arrival/duration/recession, probability, CRS/resolution, licence and NoData. Keep pluvial, buitendijkse and indirect network pathways separately typed.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated presets reuse one complete 136-neighbourhood order.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire all rank Schouw, Jagersveld, Karveel West, Flevobos and Visvijverbos first. Flevobos and Visvijverbos have zero official residents yet rank fourth/fifth for flood, heat and cyber, while Hollandse Hout is near the bottom. The same order cannot represent dike breach, street flow, heat, wind, fire/smoke, cyber targets and infrastructure.
findings.action: Replace the common municipality seed with hazard-specific source, eligible-domain, forcing, exposed-object and support adapters over full polygons. Add cross-preset tests that unrelated hazards cannot silently share all 136 ranks; preserve official zero residents while separating activity demand, and make absent spatial evidence Unknown rather than precise ordering.

findings.action: Integrate versioned municipal/Zuiderzeeland stress cases with hyetograph, AHN/BGT, street/low-storage routing, sewer-included flag, seepage/groundwater, polder receiving levels, resolution, units, licence and NoData. Join pumps/weirs/AWZI only after authority review of connectivity, native capacity, condition, settings, power/fuel/manual staffing and valid time.

Require an explicit ignition/perimeter or labelled external plume, access/firewater and suppression state; absent source is Unknown/no selected event, not zero local risk or observed smoke.

findings.action: Attach publisher, dataset/version, issue/valid/retrieval time, coverage, licence, evidence class, lifecycle, affectsSimulation, uncertainty and NoData to every layer/value/export. Use an explicit reference clock; stale/future state deactivates, missing horizons render Unknown, point data are not surfaces, and normalized inundation stress is never labelled depth/metres.

residualLimitations: Complete electricity, gas, drinking-water, sewer/drainage, telecom, care and supply topology, control logic, live load/outage, backup, crews, spares, fuel and restoration state are unavailable or security-sensitive; public geometry, plans and territories cannot replace them.

No selected Zuiderzeeland/WMCN/LIWO case establishes a GM0995 IJsselmeer/Markermeer defence breach, compartment/control state, terrain-connected footprint, depth/velocity, arrival or recession. A generic value is not evidence and no selected case is not safe.

Lelystad climate stress-test products and GRP are valuable official scenario/programme evidence but require native machine files, edition, event/antecedent state, CRS, units, licence, lifecycle and explicit NoData before analytical use.

The HWH screen contains 89 heterogeneous objects with incomplete/null capacities and no complete catchment/sewer/defence topology, settings, maintenance, power/fuel/backup, live level/state or event capacity.

Houtribsluis point observations/forecasts do not establish a spatial water boundary, dike loading, overtopping/breach or local inundation. No GM0995 T+48/T+72 point survives the forecast coverage decline; missing horizons cannot be held constant or treated as zero.

Eight NWB logical links, bridge/approach omissions, one station, 114 GTFS stops and zero NDW situations do not establish scenario-time operation, vehicle eligibility, passability, emergency priority, detours, destination or throughput.
The Houtribdijk restriction is published but starts only at an unspecified future time in autumn 2026. Applying it on 3 September would be false; ignoring it after activation would also be false.

St Jansdal/RIVM records do not expose incident-time ambulance availability, staffing, dispatch, external ED acceptance/diversion, occupancy, backup or restoration; protected operational information must not be inferred.

Current General Aviation does not validate conditional commercial or future F-35 operations. The provisional 2024 public airport plan and protected operational annexes are not live incident/resource state.

CBS residents omit pupils, patients, commuters, workers, airport users, nature visitors, volunteers and responders. Rounded/suppressed aggregates cannot identify individuals, preparedness or event presence.
One Liander planning sample is neither municipal coverage nor outage evidence, and sensitive topology must not be reconstructed publicly.
Antenna and education registers have different spatial support, cadence and licences and remain affectsSimulation=false without verified causal bindings.

Current KNMI station values and Waterinfo points are timestamped observations/forecasts, not evidence for a synthetic event. No or missing values are coverage facts rather than zero hazard or service continuity.

Exact hazard, affected-population, service, recovery and person-hour outputs remain synthetic exercises, not observations, forecasts, operator commitments or decision-grade advice until critical/high findings are corrected and authorities review the case.
This audit covers only the first 72 hours. Polder drainage, subsidence/groundwater, nature recovery, care displacement and infrastructure restoration can persist much longer.
